newsitem.title: CHINA: ATHLETICS-WORLD RECORD-HOLDER WANG SICK - REPORT.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-WORLD RECORD-HOLDER WANG SICK - REPORT.

text.p: China's record-breaking long-distance runner Wang Junxia has contracted a nervous disorder, forcing her to drop out of winter training, said an edition of the Shenzhen Business newspaper seen in Beijing on Wednesday.
Wang was diagnosed last December as having neurasthenia, a nervous condition that causes fatigue, anxiety and localised pains, the newspaper said in its January 19 edition.

The athlete, who shot to international fame in 1993 when she broke the world records in the 3,000 metres and 10,000 metres, was undergoing treatment in Shenyang in the northeastern province of Liaoning, it said.
Wang was taking daily doses of traditional Chinese medicine and was trying to maintain a convalescent training programme, it said.
"But every time she runs a lap, fierce headaches make it difficult for her to bear up," the paper said.
Wang intended to compete in the Asian Games and had her sights set on running in the world athletics championships in Athens in August.
The paper did not say if her condition would force her to pull out of either competition.
